summary: Cycle-7 focused adversarial review of KE-ENSO notebook_v2 v2.7 (per-plot linked controls + driver backgrounds)

verdicts.reviewer: hostile-ojs-plot-mechanic (node+jsdom execution vs real parquets, Machakos+Marsabit)
verdicts.verdict: v2.7's new machinery is mechanically sound almost everywhere: every §3 chart body executed in node+jsdom with the real libraries and real data across all combos (3 bgModes x 6 drivers x date/year x, 3 speiIdx, both ipcView, 3x3 priceAgg/priceView, 3 totAgg, both hsEra, bars/lines 3.6-A) with zero crashes; quarterly/yearly bucket means reproduce exactly in python (0 mismatches over 181 buckets, UTC month edges correct for end-of-month period_dates); Inputs.bind clone rows propagate both ways and mint fresh nodes per call; the 3.6-A lag-shift is correct (OND(Y-1) wash + MAM(Y) band verified in rendered tooltips and geometry, no double-shift); fence checker PASS (474 cells); all 206 nbText refs exist with en/fr; no INT64->BigInt traps in the new query paths; loader dep arrays are data-only in both directions. BUT the new year-x figures (3.3 Yearly bars, 3.7) draw their bars with `interval: 1`, which bins to [Y, Y+1) while the new backgrounds and lens outlines are centred on Y — every bar sits half a slot right of its shading, visually attributing year-Y outcomes to MAM(Y+1), and the last bar overflows the plot frame (measured 899px vs 880px frame edge). That inverts the exact season-attribution grammar v2.7 was built to deliver and should block deploy until fixed. Secondary: 3.6-A exposes lens controls and a legend promising dashed outlines it never draws; 3.7 carries no control row despite its caption claiming one.

NOT READY — the headline lag grammar of 3.6-A is correct (verified numerically: harvest 2023 sits over OND2022 z=-1.03 / MAM2023 z=+1.80; no double shift, no unshifted leak), the new background system's interpolation honesty holds, and the fence check passes. But two critical defects remain: Fig 3.1 plots the NDJ and DJF rolling windows a full year late (the parquet labels them by END year, the centre map assumes start year — the chart shows a false drought dip in the middle of the 1997-98 and 2023-24 El Niño peaks), and the new linear-x yearly bars (3.3 Yearly, 3.7) sit on [Y, Y+1] instead of centered on tick Y, so every bar visually overlaps the WRONG season halves (OND(Y)+MAM(Y+1)) and the last bar overflows the frame — this silently breaks the exact season-position grammar the v2.7 backgrounds were built to convey. Three majors (a county-generic caption asserting a 2020-23 SPEI-12 deficit that is false for ~29 of 47 counties; Western-V shading offered on OND seasons against the notebook's own framing; Fig 3.7 claiming linked controls it does not carry) plus minors.

confirmed.title: Year-x bars offset half a slot from their season backgrounds; last bar overflows the frame (3.3 Yearly bars, 3.7)

Every bar is drawn half a slot to the right of its year tick and its own background: the right half of a year-Y bar sits over the MAM(Y+1) background band, so a 2021 drought-report bar is visually underlaid by 2022's long-rains driver state — the exact season-misattribution the lag-grammar rules exist to prevent. The MAM lens outline for year Y never touches year Y's bar at all. Additionally the final bar's bin extends to yEnd+1 while the x domain ends at yEnd+0.5, and rects are not clipped, so the last bar paints into the right margin past the axis.

confirmed.fix: Replace `x: "year", interval: 1` with explicit centred edges: `x1: (d) => d.year - 0.5, x2: (d) => d.year + 0.5` (keep the insets) in both Plot.rectY calls. confirmed.title: 3.6-A ignores the lens controls its own cloned row exposes, while its legend promises lens outlines

confirmed.title: Fig 3.1: NDJ and DJF SPEI windows plotted 12 months late
confirmed.where: notebook_v2.qmd lines 3752-3762 (speiRows centre map: NDJ: [12, 0], DJF: [1, 1])
confirmed.problem: chirps_county labels year-crossing rolling windows by the END year (NDJ 1998 = Nov 1997 - Jan 1998), but the centre map assumes start-year labelling, placing NDJ-Y at Dec Y and DJF-Y at Jan Y+1. Every Dec-15 and Jan-15 point on the Fig 3.1 strip therefore carries the PREVIOUS winter's SPEI value, for all three selectable windows.
confirmed.evidence: Marsabit SPEI-03: OND 1997 = +1.75 (El Nino peak) but NDJ 1997 = +0.08 and DJF 1997 = -0.92, while NDJ 1998 = +1.07, DJF 1998 = +2.10, JFM 1998 = +1.98 — only the end-year reading is physically coherent. Same pattern 2023-24 (OND 2023 = +1.69, DJF 2023 = -1.19, DJF 2024 = +1.06) and on SPEI-12. As coded, the chart dives from +1.69 to -1.19 in mid-January 2024, inside the wettest OND on record, and the hover mislabels the window the reader infers.
confirmed.fix: Change the centre map to NDJ: [12, -1] (centre Dec of year-1) and DJF: [1, 0] (centre Jan of year Y). Then re-verify visually that the 1997-98 and 2023-24 wet spikes are monotone through the turn of the year.

verify.reasoning: CONFIRMED by direct recomputation from the served parquets. (1) Quoted code is accurate: notebook_v2.qmd lines 3752-3762 (speiRows) contain the centre map with `NDJ: [12, 0], DJF: [1, 1]` on lines 3753-3754, i.e. NDJ-Y plotted at Dec 15 of Y and DJF-Y at Jan 15 of Y+1 (start-year assumption; the cell comment at 3749-3751 even states "DJF centres on Jan of the following year"). (2) chirps_county is END-year labelled: decomposing every PTOT period against chirps_county_monthly across all 47 counties, 11 of 12 rolling periods match the end-year window EXACTLY (DJF: 2160/2160 rows, MAE=0.0000, DJF-Y = Dec(Y-1)+Jan(Y)+Feb(Y)), while the start-year hypothesis fails (Marsabit DJF MAE=61.8). (3) Fig 3.1 plots SPEI, and SPEI is also end-year labelled: SPEI-03 DJF-Y correlates r=+0.656 with Dec(Y-1)-Feb(Y) rainfall vs r=-0.150 with Dec(Y)-Feb(Y+1); SPEI-03 NDJ-Y r=+0.646 with Nov(Y-1)-Jan(Y) vs r=+0.106 with Nov(Y)-Jan(Y+1) (SON same-year sanity r=0.495). (4) Every SPEI-03 number quoted in the finding reproduces exactly (Marsabit: OND 1997=1.75, NDJ 1997=0.08, DJF 1997=-0.92, NDJ 1998=1.07, DJF 1998=2.10, JFM 1998=1.98; OND 2023=1.69, DJF 2023=-1.19, DJF 2024=1.06) — only end-year labelling is physically coherent through the 1997-98 and 2023-24 El Niño peaks. (5) The centre map is variable-independent, so the 12-month displacement affects all three selectable windows (speiIdxOpts = SPEI-03/06/12, line 2819). SIDE DISCOVERY (does not refute; separate upstream bug): the PTOT NDJ series in chirps_county.parquet is itself corrupt — lstsq decomposition over 2064 county-years gives NDJ-Y = Nov(Y) + Dec(Y-1) + Jan(Y) with R²=1.0 and max residual 4.5e-12, a NON-contiguous window (Nov taken from the wrong year). SPEI NDJ does not share this defect (its correlation profile matches the correct end-year window), and the notebook never queries PTOT NDJ (PTOT is only used with OND/MAM/annual), so Fig 3.1's diagnosis stands as stated.
verify.fix: The proposed fix is correct and sufficient for Fig 3.1: in notebook_v2.qmd line 3753-3754 change `NDJ: [12, 0]` to `NDJ: [12, -1]` (centre Dec of Y-1) and `DJF: [1, 1]` to `DJF: [1, 0]` (centre Jan of Y); all ten other entries are already correct under end-year labelling (their spans and centres never cross the year boundary). Two amendments: (a) also rewrite the misleading cell comment at lines 3749-3751 — replace "(DJF centres on Jan of the following year)" with a statement that chirps_county labels year-crossing windows by the END year (NDJ 1998 = Nov 1997-Jan 1998), verified by exact decomposition against chirps_county_monthly; (b) file a separate upstream/pipeline issue (D409 staging, not a notebook edit): the PTOT NDJ series in chirps_county.parquet is corrupt — exactly Nov(Y)+Dec(Y-1)+Jan(Y), a non-contiguous window — currently unconsumed by the notebook but a trap for any future use; SPEI NDJ is unaffected. After the edit, re-verify visually that the 1997-98 and 2023-24 wet spikes are monotone through the turn of the year, as the finding suggests.

confirmed.title: Static caption asserts a 2020-23 SPEI-12 deficit that is false for half the counties
confirmed.where: nbText_v2.json line 498 (b3.seasonStripCaption), rendered at notebook_v2.qmd line 1152
confirmed.problem: "The 2020-23 event shows as the long unbroken deficit on the 12-month window" is a county-specific pattern claim in a caption shown identically for all 47 counties. It is false for the entire western belt.
confirmed.evidence: From chirps_county SPEI-12, Jun 2020 - Dec 2023: 29 of 48 admin units have a longest consecutive negative run under 12 months; Kakamega, Kisumu, Siaya, Vihiga, Nandi, Kericho, Kisii, Nyamira, Migori, Narok have ZERO negative months. Only Mandera reaches a 24+ month unbroken run.
confirmed.fix: Scope the sentence (e.g. "In the arid north and east — Marsabit, Mandera, Turkana — the 2020-23 event shows as a long deficit on the 12-month window; humid western counties barely register it"), or compute the deficit-run sentence live per county and drop it when the run is short.

verify.reasoning: Every element verified by execution. (1) Quoted line: /Users/pstewarda/Documents/rprojects/atlas_nb-KE-enso/data/KE-enso-explorer/nbText_v2.json line 498 defines b3.seasonStripCaption whose en string contains verbatim "The 2020–23 event shows as the long unbroken deficit on the 12-month window." — confirmed both by sed and by json.load, so it is the effective parsed value. (2) Render site: notebook_v2.qmd line 1152 renders it via plotFooter(_lang(nbText.sections.b3.seasonStripCaption), ...); _lang selects only by language, never by county, so all 47 counties get the identical sentence. (3) Data claim recomputed from chirps_county.parquet using the notebook's own centre-month mapping (qmd lines 3749-3762) for SPEI-12, window Jun 2020 - Dec 2023: 48 admin units; exactly 29 have a longest consecutive negative run under 12 months; all ten named western counties (Kakamega, Kisumu, Siaya, Vihiga, Nandi, Kericho, Kisii, Nyamira, Migori, Narok) have ZERO negative SPEI-12 months in the window (plus Bomet and Homa Bay, so 12 counties total at zero); only Mandera reaches a 24+ month run (26 months; next are Kiambu/Laikipia/West Pokot at 23). For roughly a quarter of counties the caption asserts a "long unbroken deficit" over a period in which the chart shows no deficit at all — a real, county-visible factual error, so [major] stands.
verify.fix: The proposed fix is directionally right but its example county list needs one amendment: Marsabit does NOT belong in the exemplar list (its longest SPEI-12 negative run in the window is under 15 months and it is not among the top runs; the data-supported exemplars are Mandera 26 mo, Kiambu/Laikipia/West Pokot 23 mo, Turkana 21 mo). Two acceptable fixes: (a) Static scoping in nbText_v2.json line 498 — replace the sentence with e.g. "In the drier north and east — Mandera, Turkana, West Pokot — the 2020–23 drought shows as a long unbroken deficit on the 12-month window; the humid western highlands barely registered it." (b) Better, dynamic: speiRows is already in the OJS graph at the plotFooter call (qmd line 1152), so compute the longest negative run from speiRows and append the 2020–23 sentence only when speiIdx.v === 'SPEI-12' and the run within Jun 2020–Dec 2023 is >= 12 months; this also fixes the secondary problem that the static sentence claims a 12-month-window pattern even while the user is viewing SPEI-3 or SPEI-6.

The bar also stretches the x scale ~7 months past the background (bgMarks is clamped to the data extent), leaving a bar jutting into unshaded space.
minors.evidence: python cross-check output: last data month 2026-05-31; last yearly bar x2 = 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z; last quarterly bar x2 = 2026-07-01. Bucket means/n themselves verified exact (70 quarterly + 18 yearly price buckets, 74+19 ToT buckets, 0 mismatches).
minors.fix: Clamp the final bucket's x2 to the end of the last data month (e.g. x2: new Date(Math.min(+x2, +d3.utcMonth.offset(d3.max(rows, (d) => d._t), 1)))) or visually flag partial buckets (reduced fillOpacity + '(partial)' in the title when the bucket end exceeds the data end).

minors.title: Lens-outline legend gated on the wrong condition: outlines can render with no legend, and legend can promise outlines that don't exist
minors.problem: simMarks draws dashed lens outlines whenever simYearSet is non-empty, independent of bgMode; bgLegend returns an empty span whenever bgMode === 'Off'. So with background Off + an active lens (a natural reading mode: outlines only), every §3 chart shows dashed outlines with no legend anywhere explaining them. Conversely with a background on and lens at 'All years', the legend's '· dashed outlines = the lens seasons' describes marks that aren't drawn.
minors.evidence: bgLegend line 2914: `if (bgMode === "Off") return html``;` — while simMarks (line 2932) checks only `simYearSet.size`. Executed in harness: bgMode='Off' + seasonLens='Drier than usual' renders outline rects (11 for Machakos OND) with bgLegend returning the empty span.
minors.fix: Restructure bgLegend to compose two independent parts: the driver-gradient part shown when bgMode != 'Off', and the dashed-outline note shown when simYearSet.size > 0 — returning the empty span only when both are absent.
